## MSA-Based Prediction

While Chai-1 performs well in single-sequence mode, evolutionary information via Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs) can significantly improve performance [examples/msas/README.md:1-3]().

### The `.aligned.pqt` Format
Chai-1 uses a custom Parquet-based format for MSAs which extends the standard `a3m` format with metadata required for featurization and multimer pairing [examples/msas/README.md:5-12]().

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `sequence` | Alignment hits in `a3m` format. |
| `source_database` | Origin database (`uniprot`, `uniref90`, `bfd_uniclust`, `mgnify`, or `query`). |
| `pairing_key` | String used to pair alignments across different chains (e.g., species ID). |
| `comment` | Metadata ignored by the model. |

Sources: [examples/msas/README.md:7-12]()

### MSA Implementation Pattern
Users can provide MSAs by pointing to a directory containing `<HASH>.aligned.pqt` files, where the hash corresponds to the unique chain sequence [examples/msas/README.md:33-35](). Alternatively, the system supports automatic generation via the ColabFold server [examples/msas/README.md:64-71]().

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "MSA Data Flow"
        A3M[".a3m files"] --> PQT_Conv["chai a3m-to-pqt"]
        PQT_Conv --> PQT[".aligned.pqt"]
        PQT --> MSAContext["MSAContext Object"]
        MSAContext --> Inference["run_inference()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Auto-Generation"
        Fasta["Input FASTA"] --> ColabFold["ColabFold Server"]
        ColabFold --> AutoMSA["Automatic MSAContext"]
        AutoMSA --> Inference
    end
```

Sources: [examples/msas/README.md:27-35](), [examples/msas/README.md:64-71]()

## Restraints and Constraints

Chai-1 allows folding complexes with user-specified "restraints" to guide the model. These are provided as a `.csv` table specifying inter-chain contacts or pockets [examples/restraints/README.md:1-9]().

### Restraint Types
- **Contact**: A restraint between two specific residues in distinct chains (e.g., `A R84` to `C G7`) [examples/restraints/README.md:14-15]().
- **Pocket**: A coarser restraint where a specific residue in one chain is in contact with *any* residue in another chain [examples/restraints/README.md:16-17]().

### Restraint Data Mapping
Chains are identified alphabetically (A, B, C...) based on their order in the FASTA file. Residues are specified using a 1-indexed notation like `D4` (Aspartate at position 4) [examples/restraints/README.md:19-20]().

Sources: [examples/restraints/README.md:7-22](), [examples/restraints/contact.restraints:1-3](), [examples/restraints/pocket.restraints:1-4]()

## Covalent Bond Examples

Covalent bonds can be specified to model glycosylation or non-canonical linkages between ligands and proteins [examples/covalent_bonds/README.md:1-4]().

### Glycan Specification
Chai-1 uses a recursive parenthetical syntax in the FASTA file to define glycan branching and a restraints file to define the attachment point to the protein [examples/covalent_bonds/README.md:32-62]().

**Example Branched Glycan FASTA:**
`NAG(4-1 NAG(4-1 BMA(3-1 MAN)(6-1 MAN)))` [examples/covalent_bonds/README.md:60-61]()

### Bond Restraint Logic
The restraint file links specific atoms (e.g., `@N` on a protein residue to `@C1` on a glycan ring) [examples/covalent_bonds/README.md:27-29]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Code Entities"
        AAStructure["AllAtomStructureContext"]
        DropAtoms["drop_glycan_leaving_atoms_inplace"]
        InfFunc["run_inference"]
    end

    subgraph "Input Data"
        FastaBond[">glycan sequence with (4-1) syntax"]
        CSVRestraint["covalent connection_type in CSV"]
    end

    FastaBond --> InfFunc
    CSVRestraint --> InfFunc
    InfFunc --> AAStructure
    AAStructure --> DropAtoms
    DropAtoms --"Removes OH groups"--> FinalCoord["Final 3D Coordinates"]
```

Sources: [examples/covalent_bonds/README.md:25-29](), [examples/covalent_bonds/README.md:47-50](), [examples/covalent_bonds/README.md:76-78]()

### Non-Glycan Covalent Ligands
For ligands defined via SMILES, the user must provide a SMILES string *without* the leaving atoms and specify the bond in the restraints file [examples/covalent_bonds/README.md:70-78]().

**Example Restraint for Ligand Bond:**
`A,C217@SG,B,@S1,covalent,1.0,0.0,0.0,protein-ligand,bond1` [examples/covalent_bonds/8cyo.restraints:1-3]()

Sources: [examples/covalent_bonds/8cyo.fasta:1-4](), [examples/covalent_bonds/predict_covalent_ligand.py:16-25]()

This page provides essential information for developers contributing to the `chai-lab` codebase. It covers the repository structure, development environment setup, key utilities, and coding standards. This guide assumes you are familiar with Python development and want to contribute code, fix bugs, or extend the system.

For end-users looking to use Chai-1 for structure prediction, please refer to [Getting Started](#2). For detailed information on specific development topics, see the subsections: [Type System](#9.1), [Testing Framework](#9.2), and [CI/CD Pipeline](#9.3).

## Repository Structure

The Chai Lab repository follows a modular organization designed to separate concerns and maintain clean interfaces between components.

**Repository Organization Diagram**

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Repository Root"
        MainPackage["chai_lab/"]
        License["LICENSE"]
        Reqs["requirements.in"]
        Docker["Dockerfile.chailab"]
        Workflows[".github/workflows/"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Package"

    end
```

## Development Environment

To work on the `chai-lab` codebase, you can use the provided `Dockerfile.chailab` to ensure a consistent environment. The environment is based on Ubuntu 22.04 and uses `uv` for fast dependency management [Dockerfile.chailab:1-75]().

### Docker Environment Configuration
The development container sets up several important environment variables to manage caches and Python behavior:

| Variable | Value | Purpose |
|----------|-------|---------|
| `MYPY_CACHE_DIR` | `/tmp/.chai_lab_mypy_cache` | Keeps large mypy cache outside the working tree [Dockerfile.chailab:11-11]() |
| `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX` | `/tmp/.chai_lab_pycache` | Keeps `__pycache__` out of the source tree [Dockerfile.chailab:17-17]() |
| `PYTHONFAULTHANDLER` | `1` | Prints tracebacks after segfaults [Dockerfile.chailab:15-15]() |
| `VIRTUAL_ENV` | `/opt/venv` | Location of the virtual environment [Dockerfile.chailab:60-60]() |

Sources: [Dockerfile.chailab:1-85]()


# Page: Type System

# Type System

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [LICENSE](LICENSE)
- [chai_lab/__init__.py](chai_lab/__init__.py)
- [chai_lab/utils/typing.py](chai_lab/utils/typing.py)

</details>



This page documents the type checking infrastructure and validation utilities used throughout the Chai Lab codebase. The system ensures code correctness by validating data types both during development and at runtime, specifically focusing on the complex tensor shapes and multidimensional array operations used in the Chai-1 molecular structure prediction pipeline.

## Overview

Chai Lab employs a hybrid type checking approach that combines static type annotations with runtime type checking. This system is particularly valuable for catching errors in tensor shapes, dimensions, and data types which are critical in scientific computing applications like molecular modeling.

The type system is built on two specialized libraries:
- **beartype**: A high-performance runtime type checker for Python.
- **jaxtyping**: A type annotation system for JAX (and by extension, compatible tensor) arrays that provides shape and dtype checking.

## Type System Architecture

The following diagram illustrates how the type system is structured within the Chai Lab codebase, specifically focusing on the `typecheck` decorator logic.

**Diagram: Type System Validation Flow**
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Requirements"
        Req["Need 3D coordinates for atoms [N, 3]"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space: chai_lab.utils.typing"
        TypeDec["typecheck decorator"]
        Flag["should_typecheck flag"]
        JaxTyped["jaxtyped"]
        BearType["beartype"]
        JaxCheck["jaxtyping checks"]
    end

    Req -->|"Implemented as"| FuncSig["Function Signature with jaxtyping annotations"]
    FuncSig --> TypeDec
    TypeDec -->|"Checks"| Flag
    
    Flag -->|"True"| JaxTyped
    Flag -->|"False"| NoOp["Return original function"]
    
    JaxTyped -->|"Uses"| BearType
    JaxTyped -->|"Uses"| JaxCheck
    
    BearType -->|"Validates"| ScalarArgs["Scalar & Object Types"]
    JaxCheck -->|"Validates"| TensorShapes["Tensor Shapes & Dtypes"]
```
Sources: [chai_lab/utils/typing.py:23-33](), [chai_lab/utils/typing.py:7-19]()

## Core Components

### The `typecheck` Decorator
The primary entry point for the type system is the `typecheck` decorator defined in `chai_lab/utils/typing.py`. It serves as a wrapper that conditionally enables runtime validation.

- **Implementation**: If `should_typecheck` is `True`, it returns the function or class wrapped by `jaxtyped(typechecker=beartype)`. Otherwise, it returns the original object with no runtime overhead [chai_lab/utils/typing.py:29-33]().
- **Scope**: It can be applied to both functions and classes [chai_lab/utils/typing.py:29-29]().

### Configuration: `should_typecheck`
The global flag `should_typecheck` controls the enforcement of types. 
- **Persistence**: Because modules are only loaded once, the value of `should_typecheck` remains constant over the lifetime of the program [chai_lab/utils/typing.py:21-23]().
- **Default**: It is currently set to `True` [chai_lab/utils/typing.py:23-23]().

### Re-exported Tensor Type Aliases
To provide a unified interface, `chai_lab.utils.typing` re-exports several key types from `jaxtyping`. These are used to annotate tensors (typically JAX or PyTorch arrays) throughout the model trunk and feature generation pipelines.

| Alias | Underlying jaxtyping Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Bool` | `jaxtyping.Bool` | Boolean array/tensor |
| `Float` | `jaxtyping.Float` | Generic floating-point array |
| `Float32` | `jaxtyping.Float32` | 32-bit floating-point array |
| `Int` | `jaxtyping.Int` | Generic integer array |
| `Int32` | `jaxtyping.Int32` | 32-bit integer array |
| `UInt8` | `jaxtyping.UInt8` | 8-bit unsigned integer array |
| `Num` | `jaxtyping.Num` | Any numeric array (int or float) |
| `Shaped` | `jaxtyping.Shaped` | Array with a specific shape but any dtype |

Sources: [chai_lab/utils/typing.py:8-19](), [chai_lab/utils/typing.py:36-48]()

## Data Flow and Validation

The following diagram bridges the gap between the internal `typing` utilities and their application in the broader system (e.g., in the Inference Engine or Feature Assembly).

**Diagram: Application of Types in Model Pipeline**
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Natural Language Domain"
        ResidueData["Residue-level features"]
        AtomCoords["3D Atom Coordinates"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Domain"
        direction TB
        Annot1["Int[N_residues]"]
        Annot2["Float[N_atoms, 3]"]
        Func["@typecheck<br/>def process_features(...)"]
        Err["TypeCheckError"]
    end

    ResidueData -.-> Annot1
    AtomCoords -.-> Annot2
    
    Annot1 --> Func
    Annot2 --> Func
    
    Func -->|"Invalid Shape/Type"| Err
    Func -->|"Valid"| Output["Result Tensor"]
```
Sources: [chai_lab/utils/typing.py:16-16](), [chai_lab/utils/typing.py:29-31]()

## Usage Patterns

### Function Decoration
Functions requiring strict shape validation are decorated with `@typecheck`. This is standard for functions handling MSA (Multiple Sequence Alignment) data, structural templates, or diffusion coordinates where dimensions like `[batch, atoms, 3]` must be strictly maintained.

```python
from chai_lab.utils.typing import typecheck, Float, Int32

@typecheck
def compute_loss(
    predictions: Float[..., "atoms", 3], 
    targets: Float[..., "atoms", 3],
    mask: Int32[..., "atoms"]
) -> Float[()]:
    ...
```

### Error Handling
When a type or shape mismatch occurs at runtime, the system raises a `TypeCheckError` [chai_lab/utils/typing.py:16-16](). This exception is re-exported in the `__all__` list of the typing utility for easy catching during testing or debugging [chai_lab/utils/typing.py:38-38]().

## Implementation Details

The core implementation in `chai_lab/utils/typing.py` is concise, leveraging the interoperability between `beartype` (for standard Python types) and `jaxtyping` (for array-specific logic).

```python
def typecheck(cls_or_func: Func) -> Func:
    if should_typecheck:
        return jaxtyped(typechecker=beartype)(cls_or_func)  # type: ignore
    else:
        return cls_or_func
```
Sources: [chai_lab/utils/typing.py:29-33]()

The use of `typing.TypeVar("Func")` ensures that the decorator maintains the type signature of the wrapped function or class for static analysis tools like `mypy` [chai_lab/utils/typing.py:26-29]().

Sources: [chai_lab/utils/typing.py:1-49]()

This document outlines the testing infrastructure and practices used in the Chai-1 molecular structure prediction system. For information about the type system used in conjunction with testing, see [Type System](9.1).

## Overview

The Chai-1 codebase uses pytest as its primary testing framework to verify component functionality and ensure system reliability. Tests cover input parsing, molecular conformer generation, tool integration, dataset collation, and restraint handling. All tests are integrated into the development workflow through automated continuous integration processes.

```mermaid
graph TD
    TestFramework["Chai-1 Testing Framework"] --> pytest["pytest"]
    pytest --> TestFiles["Test Files<br>(tests/*.py)"]
    TestFramework --> CI["CI Integration<br>(GitHub Actions)"]
    CI --> AutoExec["Automated Test Execution"]
    
    TestFiles --> ParsingTests["test_parsing.py<br>FASTA & entity validation"]
    TestFiles --> InferenceDatasetTests["test_inference_dataset.py<br>Chain loading & tokenization"]
    TestFiles --> RestraintTests["test_restraints.py<br>Contact & pocket restraints"]
    TestFiles --> MSATests["test_msa_*.py<br>A3M tokenization & pairing"]
    TestFiles --> ExampleInputs["example_inputs.py<br>Test data fixtures"]
```

Sources: [.github/workflows/pytest.yml:1-31](), [tests/test_parsing.py:1-80](), [tests/test_inference_dataset.py:1-124](), [tests/test_restraints.py:1-126]()

## Test Directory Structure

Tests are organized in the `tests/` directory at the repository root. The testing framework follows standard pytest conventions:

1. Test files follow the naming convention `test_*.py` for automatic discovery.
2. Each test file focuses on testing a specific component or module.
3. Test functions use the `test_` prefix naming convention.
4. Shared test data is organized in helper modules like `example_inputs.py` [tests/example_inputs.py:6-38]().

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class "tests/" {
        test_parsing.py
        test_inference_dataset.py
        test_restraints.py
        test_msa_a3m_tokenization.py
        example_inputs.py
    }
    
    class "test_parsing.py" {
        +test_simple_protein_fasta()
        +test_modified_protein_fasta()
        +test_parsing()
    }
    
    class "test_inference_dataset.py" {
        +test_malformed_smiles()
        +test_ions_parsing()
        +test_protein_with_smiles()
    }
    
    class "test_restraints.py" {
        +test_loading_restraints()
        +test_restraints_with_manual_chain_names()
    }
    
    "tests/" --> "test_parsing.py": contains
    "tests/" --> "test_inference_dataset.py": contains
    "tests/" --> "test_restraints.py": contains
    "test_parsing.py" --> "example_inputs.py": imports
```

Sources: [tests/test_parsing.py:1-80](), [tests/test_inference_dataset.py:1-124](), [tests/test_restraints.py:1-126](), [tests/example_inputs.py:1-38]()

## Continuous Integration

Tests run automatically via GitHub Actions as defined in the `pytest.yml` workflow configuration [.github/workflows/pytest.yml:1-31](). The CI pipeline is triggered on pushes to `main` and all pull requests.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    CodeChange["Code Change<br>(Push to main or PR)"] --> GitHubActions["GitHub Actions<br>pytest.yml workflow"]
    GitHubActions --> UbuntuSetup["Setup Ubuntu Environment"]
    UbuntuSetup --> SysDeps["Install System Dependencies<br>sudo apt-get install kalign"]
    SysDeps --> PythonSetup["Setup Python 3.10<br>with pip cache"]
    PythonSetup --> TorchInstall["Install CPU-only PyTorch<br>--extra-index-url pytorch.org"]
    TorchInstall --> UVInstall["Install dependencies with uv<br>filter out nvidia packages"]
    UVInstall --> RunTests["Run pytest ./tests/"]
    RunTests --> TestResult{"Tests Pass?"}
    TestResult -->|"Yes"| WorkflowSuccess["Workflow Succeeds"]
    TestResult -->|"No"| WorkflowFail["Workflow Fails"]
```

### CI Configuration Details

| Configuration | Value | Purpose |
|---------------|-------|---------|
| Python Version | 3.10 | Ensures compatibility with minimum supported version [ .github/workflows/pytest.yml:19]() |
| PyTorch Version | CPU-only | Allows testing in GPU-free environments [.github/workflows/pytest.yml:24]() |
| Package Manager | uv | Fast dependency resolution and installation [.github/workflows/pytest.yml:24-26]() |
| System Dependencies | kalign | Required for sequence alignment tests [.github/workflows/pytest.yml:15]() |

Sources: [.github/workflows/pytest.yml:1-31]()

## Test Implementation Patterns

### Input Parsing and Entity Identification

The `test_parsing.py` module verifies that the system correctly identifies molecular types and parses FASTA headers.

- **Entity Types**: Validates `EntityType` identification for proteins, DNA, RNA, and ligands [tests/test_parsing.py:45-57]().
- **Modified Sequences**: Ensures `constituents_of_modified_fasta` correctly handles bracketed residues like `(KCJ)` or `(SEP)` [tests/test_parsing.py:24-28]().
- **SMILES**: Confirms FASTA-formatted SMILES strings are correctly read [tests/test_parsing.py:73-80]().

### Inference Dataset and Tokenization

The `test_inference_dataset.py` module tests the conversion of raw inputs into `Chain` objects and `AllAtomStructureContext`.

- **Malformed Inputs**: Verifies that malformed SMILES (e.g., "Zn" instead of "[Zn+2]") are dropped during chain loading [tests/test_inference_dataset.py:29-43]().
- **Ions**: Ensures ions like `[Mg+2]` carry the correct charge and atomic number (element 12) in the structure context [tests/test_inference_dataset.py:52-61]().
- **Merging**: Tests the `AllAtomStructureContext.merge` function to ensure multiple chains (proteins and ligands) are correctly combined into a single context [tests/test_inference_dataset.py:80-82]().

### Restraints and Feature Collation

The `test_restraints.py` module tests the end-to-end flow from restraint parsing to feature generation.

- **Chain Mapping**: `test_restraints_with_manual_chain_names` verifies that restraints are correctly mapped to tokens regardless of whether automatic (A, B, C) or manual subchain IDs are used [tests/test_restraints.py:49-126]().
- **Feature Generation**: It uses the `Collate` class and `chai1.feature_factory` to ensure that `TokenDistanceRestraint` and `TokenPairPocketRestraint` features are populated in the batch [tests/test_restraints.py:105-116]().

Sources: [tests/test_parsing.py:24-80](), [tests/test_inference_dataset.py:29-107](), [tests/test_restraints.py:49-126]()

## Running Tests Locally

To run tests locally, follow the setup pattern used in CI:

1. **Install system dependencies**:
   ```bash
   sudo apt-get install kalign  # On Ubuntu/Debian
   ```

2. **Install dependencies** (using `uv` for speed, as seen in CI):
   ```bash
   uv pip install -r requirements.in
   uv pip install -r requirements.dev
   uv pip install -e .
   ```

3. **Run pytest**:
   ```bash
   pytest ./tests/
   ```

### Targeted Testing

```bash
# Run specific test file
pytest tests/test_inference_dataset.py

# Run specific test function
pytest tests/test_inference_dataset.py::test_ions_parsing

# Run with verbose output
pytest ./tests/ -v
```

Sources: [.github/workflows/pytest.yml:22-30](), [tests/test_inference_dataset.py:52-61]()

## Key Test Components

| Component | Test File | Description |
|-----------|-----------|-------------|
| FASTA Parsing | `test_parsing.py` | Validates `read_fasta` and `constituents_of_modified_fasta` [tests/test_parsing.py:59-71](). |
| Dataset Loading | `test_inference_dataset.py` | Tests `load_chains_from_raw` and `AllAtomResidueTokenizer` [tests/test_inference_dataset.py:12-26](). |
| Restraints | `test_restraints.py` | Tests `parse_pairwise_table` and restraint feature mapping [tests/test_restraints.py:31-38](). |
| MSA Processing | `test_msa_a3m_tokenization.py` | Tests `tokenize_sequences_to_arrays` and insertion handling [tests/test_msa_a3m_tokenization.py:10-37](). |
| Alignment | `test_kalign.py` | Tests `kalign_query_to_reference` tool integration [tests/test_kalign.py:5-17](). |

Sources: [tests/test_parsing.py:1-80](), [tests/test_inference_dataset.py:1-124](), [tests/test_restraints.py:1-126](), [tests/test_msa_a3m_tokenization.py:1-37](), [tests/test_kalign.py:1-17]()

This document describes the continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) infrastructure for the chai-lab repository. The CI/CD pipeline ensures code quality, type safety, and automated deployment through GitHub Actions workflows and Docker containerization.

For information about the testing framework that integrates with these CI/CD processes, see [Testing Framework](#9.2).

## Pipeline Overview

The chai-lab CI/CD pipeline consists of five main components: code quality checks, type checking, automated unit testing, automated PyPI publishing, and Docker containerization. All workflows are triggered by pushes to the main branch and pull requests.

**CI/CD Pipeline Architecture**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Triggers"
        PushMain["Push to main branch"]
        PullRequest["Pull request"]
        Release["Release created"]
    end

        RuffWorkflow["ruff.yml<br/>Code formatting & linting"]
        MypyWorkflow["mypy.yml<br/>Type checking"]
        PytestWorkflow["pytest.yml<br/>Unit Testing"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Deployment"
        PyPiWorkflow["publish-to-pypi.yml<br/>Package publishing"]
        DockerBuild["Dockerfile.chailab<br/>Container image"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Environments"
        PyPiRegistry["PyPI Registry"]
        ContainerRegistry["Container Registry"]
    end
    
    PushMain --> RuffWorkflow
    PushMain --> MypyWorkflow
    PushMain --> PytestWorkflow
    PullRequest --> RuffWorkflow
    PullRequest --> MypyWorkflow
    PullRequest --> PytestWorkflow
    Release --> PyPiWorkflow
    
    RuffWorkflow --> PyPiRegistry
    MypyWorkflow --> PyPiRegistry
    PytestWorkflow --> PyPiRegistry
    PyPiWorkflow --> PyPiRegistry
    DockerBuild --> ContainerRegistry
```

Sources: [.github/workflows/ruff.yml](), [.github/workflows/mypy.yml](), [.github/workflows/pytest.yml](), [.github/workflows/publish-to-pypi.yml](), [Dockerfile.chailab]()

## Code Quality Checks

The `ruff` workflow enforces code formatting and linting standards across the entire codebase. It runs on every push to main and every pull request using pre-commit hooks.

**Ruff Workflow Process**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "ruff_workflow" ["Ruff Workflow"]
        Checkout["actions/checkout@v4"]
        SetupPython["actions/setup-python@v5<br/>Python 3.10"]
        InstallPrecommit["pip install pre-commit"]
        InstallDevDeps["pip install -r requirements.dev"]
        PrecommitInstall["pre-commit install -f"]
        RunRuff["pre-commit run ruff --all-files"]
        RunRuffFormat["pre-commit run ruff-format --all-files"]
    end
    
    Checkout --> SetupPython
    SetupPython --> InstallPrecommit
    InstallPrecommit --> InstallDevDeps
    InstallDevDeps --> PrecommitInstall
    PrecommitInstall --> RunRuff
    RunRuff --> RunRuffFormat
```

The workflow executes the following key steps:

| Step | Command | Purpose |
|------|---------|---------|
| Setup | `pip install pre-commit` | Install pre-commit framework |
| Dependencies | `pip install -r requirements.dev` | Install development dependencies |
| Configuration | `pre-commit install -f` | Configure pre-commit hooks |
| Linting | `pre-commit run ruff --all-files` | Run code linting checks via `ruff` |
| Formatting | `pre-commit run ruff-format --all-files` | Verify code formatting via `ruff-format` |

Sources: [.github/workflows/ruff.yml:20-28](), [.pre-commit-config.yaml:3-10]()

## Type Checking

The `mypy` workflow performs static type checking to ensure type safety across the codebase. It installs dependencies efficiently by separating PyTorch installation from other requirements and uses `uv` for speed.

**MyPy Workflow Process**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "mypy_workflow" ["MyPy Workflow"]
        Checkout["actions/checkout@v4"]
        SetupPython["actions/setup-python@v5<br/>Python 3.10"]
        InstallTorch["pip install torch (CPU-only)"]
        InstallUV["pip install uv"]
        InstallRequirements["uv pip install requirements"]
        InstallDevRequirements["uv pip install requirements.dev"]
        InstallPackage["uv pip install --no-deps -e ."]
        RunMypy["mypy ."]
    end
    
    Checkout --> SetupPython
    SetupPython --> InstallTorch
    InstallTorch --> InstallUV
    InstallUV --> InstallRequirements
    InstallRequirements --> InstallDevRequirements
    InstallDevRequirements --> InstallPackage
    InstallPackage --> RunMypy
```

The workflow uses a sophisticated dependency installation strategy:

- **PyTorch CPU-only**: [.github/workflows/mypy.yml:23]() installs PyTorch from the CPU-only index to avoid large GPU dependencies.
- **Filtered requirements**: [.github/workflows/mypy.yml:25]() excludes `nvidia` and `torch` packages during main installation to optimize runner time.
- **Mypy Configuration**: Mypy is configured in `pyproject.toml` to check untyped definitions [.tool.mypy:26]() and ignore missing imports for specific external packages like `rdkit`, `scipy`, and `modelcif` [.tool.mypy:29-51]().

Sources: [.github/workflows/mypy.yml:21-29](), [pyproject.toml:25-51]()

## Automated Testing

The `pytest` workflow ensures functional correctness by running the test suite on every change.

**Pytest Workflow Process**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "pytest_workflow" ["Pytest Workflow"]
        Checkout["actions/checkout@v4"]
        InstallApt["apt-get install kalign"]
        SetupPython["actions/setup-python@v5<br/>Python 3.10"]
        InstallDeps["uv pip install dependencies"]
        RunTests["pytest ./tests/"]
    end
    
    Checkout --> InstallApt
    InstallApt --> SetupPython
    SetupPython --> InstallDeps
    InstallDeps --> RunTests
```

The workflow specifically installs `kalign` [.github/workflows/pytest.yml:15](), which is required for structural template alignment tests like `test_all_matches` in `tests/test_kalign.py` [tests/test_kalign.py:8-17]().

Sources: [.github/workflows/pytest.yml:10-30](), [tests/test_kalign.py:1-17]()

## Release Pipeline

The PyPI publishing workflow automatically deploys new versions when GitHub releases are created. It includes version validation to ensure consistency between git tags and package versions.

**PyPI Publishing Workflow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "publish_workflow" ["PyPI Publishing Workflow"]
        ReleaseCreated["Release created trigger"]
        Checkout["actions/checkout@v4"]
        SetupPython["actions/setup-python@v5<br/>Python 3.10"]
        InstallDeps["pip install . && pip install hatch"]
        VersionCheck["Version validation<br/>GIT_TAG vs CODE_VERSION"]
        HatchBuild["hatch build --clean"]
        HatchPublish["hatch publish"]
    end
    
    subgraph "External"
        PyPiRegistry["PyPI Registry"]
        SecretsManager["GitHub Secrets<br/>PYPI_TOKEN"]
    end
    
    ReleaseCreated --> Checkout
    Checkout --> SetupPython
    SetupPython --> InstallDeps
    InstallDeps --> VersionCheck
    VersionCheck --> HatchBuild
    HatchBuild --> HatchPublish
    HatchPublish --> PyPiRegistry
    SecretsManager --> HatchPublish
```

The version validation process [.github/workflows/publish-to-pypi.yml:22-29]() ensures that:
- `GIT_TAG` matches the git tag from the release.
- `CODE_VERSION` matches the version defined in `chai_lab/__init__.py` (managed by `hatch version` [.tool.hatch.version:19]()).
- The workflow fails if versions don't match.

Authentication uses the `PYPI_TOKEN` secret with the `__token__` username [.github/workflows/publish-to-pypi.yml:32-33]().

Sources: [.github/workflows/publish-to-pypi.yml:1-35](), [pyproject.toml:18-19]()

## Containerization

The Docker configuration provides a complete runtime environment for chai-lab with all necessary dependencies and system tools.

**Docker Build Architecture**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "base_image" ["chailab-baseimage"]
        UbuntuBase["ubuntu:22.04"]
        SystemPackages["System packages<br/>kalign, build-essential, etc."]
        PythonSetup["Python 3.10 + dev headers"]
        CudaConfig["CUDA library linking"]
        GitConfig["Git configuration"]
    end
    
    subgraph "python_env" ["Python Environment"]
        VirtualEnv["Virtual environment<br/>/opt/venv"]
        UVInstaller["uv package manager"]
        Requirements["requirements.in installation"]
        PathConfig["PATH environment setup"]
    end
    
    subgraph "runtime_config" ["Runtime Configuration"]
        EnvVars["Environment variables<br/>PYTHONUNBUFFERED, etc."]
        CacheConfig["Cache directories<br/>mypy, pycache"]
        TimezoneConfig["Timezone configuration"]
    end
    
    UbuntuBase --> SystemPackages
    SystemPackages --> PythonSetup
    PythonSetup --> CudaConfig
    CudaConfig --> GitConfig
    GitConfig --> VirtualEnv
    VirtualEnv --> UVInstaller
    UVInstaller --> Requirements
    Requirements --> PathConfig
    PathConfig --> EnvVars
    EnvVars --> CacheConfig
    CacheConfig --> TimezoneConfig
```

Key Docker configuration elements:

| Component | Configuration | Purpose |
|-----------|---------------|---------|
| Base Image | `ubuntu:22.04` | Stable Linux foundation |
| Python | `python3.10` + `python3.10-dev` | Runtime and development headers |
| Package Manager | `uv` | Fast Python package installation |
| Virtual Environment | `/opt/venv` | Isolated Python environment |
| System Tools | `kalign`, `build-essential` | Template alignment and compilation |
| CUDA | Soft-linked libraries | GPU computation support |

Environment variables are configured for optimal Python execution:
- `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=TRUE` [Dockerfile.chailab:13]() for immediate output.
- `PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1` [Dockerfile.chailab:15]() for better debugging of segfaults.
- `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX='/tmp/.chai_lab_pycache'` [Dockerfile.chailab:17]() for clean cache management.
- `MYPY_CACHE_DIR='/tmp/.chai_lab_mypy_cache'` [Dockerfile.chailab:11]() to keep the working tree clean.

Sources: [Dockerfile.chailab:1-85]()

## Workflow Triggers and Conditions

All CI/CD workflows share consistent trigger patterns and Python version requirements:

**Trigger Configuration**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "trigger_events" ["Trigger Events"]
        MainPush["push:<br/>branches: [main]"]
        PREvent["pull_request:<br/>any PR"]
        ReleaseEvent["release:<br/>types: [created]"]
    end
    
    subgraph "workflow_matrix" ["Workflow Matrix"]
        RuffJob["ruff.yml<br/>ubuntu-latest"]
        MypyJob["mypy.yml<br/>ubuntu-latest"]
        PytestJob["pytest.yml<br/>ubuntu-latest"]
        PyPiJob["publish-to-pypi.yml<br/>ubuntu-latest"]
    end
    
    subgraph "common_config" ["Common Configuration"]
        PythonVersion["Python 3.10<br/>Minimum version"]
        PipCache["pip cache enabled"]
        UbuntuRunner["ubuntu-latest runner"]
    end
    
    MainPush --> RuffJob
    MainPush --> MypyJob
    MainPush --> PytestJob
    PREvent --> RuffJob
    PREvent --> MypyJob
    PREvent --> PytestJob
    ReleaseEvent --> PyPiJob

    MypyJob --> PythonVersion
    PytestJob --> PythonVersion
    PyPiJob --> PythonVersion

    PipCache --> UbuntuRunner
```

All workflows use Python 3.10 as the minimum version [.github/workflows/ruff.yml:18](), [.github/workflows/mypy.yml:18](), [.github/workflows/publish-to-pypi.yml:18]() with the rationale that "later versions should maintain backwards-compatibility" [.github/workflows/publish-to-pypi.yml:17]().

The `pip` cache is enabled in development workflows [.github/workflows/ruff.yml:19](), [.github/workflows/mypy.yml:19]() to speed up dependency installation during CI runs.

Sources: [.github/workflows/ruff.yml:2-8](), [.github/workflows/mypy.yml:2-8](), [.github/workflows/pytest.yml:2-8](), [.github/workflows/publish-to-pypi.yml:3-5]()

This glossary defines technical terms, internal data structures, and algorithmic concepts used throughout the Chai-1 codebase. It serves as a reference for engineers to map biological and mathematical concepts to their specific implementations in the `chai-lab` repository.

## Core Model Concepts

### Trunk Recycling
A technique where the model's trunk (the main representation-learning component) is executed multiple times, with the outputs of one pass used as inputs for the next. This allows the model to refine its internal representation before passing it to the diffusion head.
*   **Implementation**: Controlled in the inference loop within `run_folding_on_context` [chai_lab/chai1.py:1078-1091]().
*   **Sources**: [chai_lab/chai1.py:1078-1091]()

### Diffusion Loop
The process of iteratively denoising 3D coordinates from a random distribution to a structured molecular conformation. Chai-1 uses a specific noise schedule for this process.
*   **Implementation**: `InferenceNoiseSchedule` [chai_lab/model/diffusion_schedules.py:101]() is used within the sampling loop in `run_folding_on_context` [chai_lab/chai1.py:1093-1135]().
*   **Sources**: [chai_lab/chai1.py:101-1135]()

### Confidence Scoring (pLDDT, PAE, PDE)
Metrics used to estimate the quality of the predicted structure.
*   **pLDDT**: Predicted Local Distance Difference Test. Measures local confidence at the residue/token level.
*   **PAE**: Predicted Aligned Error. Estimates the error in the relative position of two residues.
*   **PDE**: Predicted Distance Error.
*   **Implementation**: Calculated in `get_scores` and `rank` [chai_lab/ranking/rank.py:104]().
*   **Sources**: [chai_lab/chai1.py:104]()

## Data Structures & Entities

### AllAtomFeatureContext
The primary "hub" object that aggregates all features required for model inference, including sequence information, MSAs, templates, and restraints.
*   **Implementation**: `AllAtomFeatureContext` [chai_lab/data/dataset/all_atom_feature_context.py:26]().
*   **Sources**: [chai_lab/chai1.py:26-27]()

### AllAtomStructureContext
Represents the structural state of a complex, including 3D coordinates, atom types, and bonding information. It is often merged from multiple `Chain` objects.
*   **Implementation**: `AllAtomStructureContext` [chai_lab/data/dataset/structure/all_atom_structure_context.py:41]().
*   **Key Method**: `merge` [tests/test_inference_dataset.py:80-82]() combines multiple chains into a single context.
*   **Sources**: [chai_lab/chai1.py:41-43](), [tests/test_inference_dataset.py:80-82]()

### PDBContext
A tensor-based representation of a molecular complex used specifically for I/O operations and PDB/CIF generation.
*   **Implementation**: `PDBContext` [chai_lab/data/io/pdb_utils.py:19-31]().
*   **Data Flow**: Converted from model output batches via `pdb_context_from_batch` [chai_lab/data/io/pdb_utils.py:48-63]().
*   **Sources**: [chai_lab/data/io/pdb_utils.py:19-63]()

### EntityType
An enumeration defining the types of molecules supported by the system.
*   **Values**: `PROTEIN`, `RNA`, `DNA`, `LIGAND`, `MANUAL_GLYCAN`.
*   **Implementation**: `EntityType` [chai_lab/data/parsing/structure/entity_type.py:100]().
*   **Sources**: [chai_lab/chai1.py:100](), [chai_lab/data/dataset/inference_dataset.py:108-127]()

## Data Formats & I/O

### .aligned.pqt (Aligned Parquet)
A specialized Parquet format used by Chai-1 to store Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs). It includes metadata like `source_database` and `pairing_key` (often a taxonomic ID) to facilitate cross-chain MSA pairing.
*   **Implementation**: `AlignedParquetModel` [chai_lab/data/parsing/msas/aligned_pqt.py:37-44]().
*   **Parsing**: `parse_aligned_pqt_to_msa_context` [chai_lab/data/parsing/msas/aligned_pqt.py:63-139]().
*   **Sources**: [chai_lab/data/parsing/msas/aligned_pqt.py:37-139]()

### .m8 (MMseqs2 Alignment Format)
A tab-separated format used to describe template hits found during a sequence search.
*   **Implementation**: Parsed by `parse_m8_file` [chai_lab/data/parsing/templates/m8.py:22-46]().
*   **Sources**: [chai_lab/data/parsing/templates/m8.py:22-46]()

### .apkl (Antipickle)
A serialization format used for caching conformers. It is a safer and more robust alternative to standard Python pickles.
*   **Usage**: Loading cached conformers in `RefConformerGenerator` [chai_lab/data/sources/rdkit.py:60-73]().
*   **Sources**: [chai_lab/data/sources/rdkit.py:60-73]()

## Feature Generation Terms

### MSAContext
Contains tokenized MSA sequences, deletion counts, and taxonomic pairing information.
*   **Implementation**: `MSAContext` [chai_lab/data/dataset/msas/msa_context.py:37]().
*   **Subsampling**: Handled by `subsample_and_reorder_msa_feats_n_mask` [chai_lab/data/dataset/msas/utils.py:51-86]().
*   **Sources**: [chai_lab/chai1.py:37-40](), [chai_lab/data/dataset/msas/utils.py:51-86]()

### RestraintContext
Encapsulates user-defined physical constraints (contacts, pockets, covalent bonds) that guide the folding process.
*   **Implementation**: `RestraintContext` [chai_lab/data/dataset/constraints/restraint_context.py:28]().
*   **Parsing**: `parse_pairwise_table` [chai_lab/data/parsing/restraints.py:173-187]().
*   **Sources**: [chai_lab/chai1.py:28-31](), [chai_lab/data/parsing/restraints.py:173-187]()

### Conformer Data
Idealized 3D coordinates and metadata (element, charge, atom names) for a single residue or ligand, typically generated via RDKit.
*   **Implementation**: `ConformerData` [chai_lab/data/parsing/structure/residue.py:21]().
*   **Generation**: `RefConformerGenerator.generate` [chai_lab/data/sources/rdkit.py:144-175]() uses `ETKDGv3` for ligands.
*   **Sources**: [chai_lab/data/sources/rdkit.py:21-175]()

## System Diagrams

### Data Mapping: Input to Code Entities
This diagram illustrates how raw user inputs (FASTA, SMILES) are transformed into internal code objects.

Structure Prediction Input Flow
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language / File Space"
        F["input.fasta"]
        S["SMILES string"]
        R["restraints.csv"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        In["Input Class [chai_lab/data/dataset/inference_dataset.py]"]
        AED["AllAtomEntityData [chai_lab/data/parsing/structure/all_atom_entity_data.py]"]
        RCG["RefConformerGenerator [chai_lab/data/sources/rdkit.py]"]
        SC["AllAtomStructureContext [chai_lab/data/dataset/structure/all_atom_structure_context.py]"]
        PI["PairwiseInteraction [chai_lab/data/parsing/restraints.py]"]
    end

    F -->|read_fasta| In
    S -->|get_lig_residues| In
    In -->|raw_inputs_to_entities_data| AED
    AED -->|AllAtomResidueTokenizer| SC
    RCG -->|provides conformers| SC
    R -->|parse_pairwise_table| PI
```
**Sources**: [chai_lab/data/dataset/inference_dataset.py:39-177](), [chai_lab/data/sources/rdkit.py:38-175](), [chai_lab/data/parsing/restraints.py:173-187]()

### Inference Pipeline: Context to Coordinates
This diagram shows the flow of data through the model components during a single inference run.

Model Execution Data Flow
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Feature Assembly"
        AFC["AllAtomFeatureContext"]
        FF["FeatureFactory [chai_lab/data/features/feature_factory.py]"]
    end

    subgraph "Model Trunk [chai_lab/chai1.py]"
        MW["ModuleWrapper"]
        TR["Trunk Recycle Loop"]
    end

    subgraph "Output Generation"
        DS["Diffusion Sampling"]
        PC["PDBContext [chai_lab/data/io/pdb_utils.py]"]
        CIF["save_to_cif [chai_lab/data/io/cif_utils.py]"]
    end

    AFC --> FF
    FF -->|forward_crop_size| MW
    MW --> TR
    TR --> DS
    DS -->|pdb_context_from_batch| PC
    PC --> CIF
```
**Sources**: [chai_lab/chai1.py:115-148](), [chai_lab/chai1.py:1078-1135](), [chai_lab/data/io/pdb_utils.py:48-63](), [chai_lab/data/io/cif_utils.py:156-172]()
